title: Brownfield context · create, refresh, recover
subtitle: One content/provenance pair per native transaction; initial finalization is separate. Existing human records retain their owners.

nodes.title: Initial population
nodes.body:
/init --brownfield → context-creation
Meaningful source; initialized marker absent
A stub is not a completed project context

nodes.title: Initialized refresh
nodes.body:
/status drift → context-check
Read-only report, then explicit scoped/full choice
Do not clear the marker or rerun initialization

nodes.title: Interrupted operation
nodes.body:
Inventory actual files, provenance and outcome
Inspect the same operation ID and native journal
Do not blindly repeat a possibly committed write

nodes.title: Qualified containment first
nodes.body:
Fresh, bound child identities
Observed host-enforced read-only profile
Generic scout role is not sufficient
Generated plugin alone does not qualify it
nodes.detail: The optional context-profile preparation helper is a repository-only CI fixture, not installed plugin capability. Caller-owned OS/tool containment, child binding, launch budgets and actual observations must be qualified before dispatch. Unknown host behavior keeps this step unavailable.

nodes.title: Bounded logical assignments
nodes.body:
Full run: six domains A–F
Scoped run: affected assignments only
Frozen source, budgets and attempt ledger
Reports only; no inline source fallback
nodes.detail: A–F cover stack, infrastructure, architecture, security, tests and data. Scope/subdivision/retries retain one run ledger and frozen source boundary. No missing or failed transport can be counted as complete coverage.

nodes.title: Validate and join reports
nodes.body:
Closed assignment/snapshot binding
48 KiB normalized join limit
Missing / failed transport → block
Recheck the source snapshot

nodes.title: Synthesize; settle relevant gaps
nodes.body:
Use joined reports, not raw source
Preserve conflicting citations
Ask material user-owned choices
Deferral is not approval

nodes.title: Five content targets
nodes.body:
CONTEXT.md • tech-stack.md
coding-standards.md
security-controls.md • code-map.md
Each with .provenance/<doc>.json

nodes.title: Finite typed preview
nodes.body:
New document or selected owned field
Current source / target identities
Exact proposed content + provenance
Unsupported human layout → refuse

nodes.title: Native approve-context reply
nodes.body:
Review this exact proposed pair
Capture actual host-observed consent
No reused approval, hash-only consent
or caller-supplied authority

nodes.title: Receipt-only native apply
nodes.body:
Qualified installed writer required
Recheck under the transaction lock
Commit document + provenance together
Read back the committed pair
nodes.detail: The context-request bridge invokes the qualified installed writer. Source-only builds do not authorize native context writes. Paired per-document atomicity does not mean all documents become visible atomically as one set.

nodes.title: Preserve other owners and human bytes
nodes.body: Task / question boards, append-only audit history, release targets and ADRs keep their own writers. No raw Write/Edit fallback on refusal.

nodes.title: Initial finalize: separate approval
nodes.body:
13 identities: five docs + five provenance
plus task board, question board, audit
Own preview → own approve-context receipt
Marker + CONTEXT provenance commit together
nodes.detail: The finalized set includes exactly the five content documents, their five v2 provenance companions, open-tasks.md, open-questions.md and overrides.log. Valid empty boards and a zero-event audit header satisfy their actual contracts. A document-write receipt never substitutes for finalization.

nodes.title: Refresh: retain initialized state
nodes.body:
Only selected pairs change
Declare scoped versus full coverage
Keep marker, human content and history
No finalization, staging or commit here

nodes.title: Recover by the same operation ID
nodes.body:
Inspect pending / committed / uncertain result
Native recover: justified complete or rollback
Committed → read back and retain
Divergence / unknown ownership → conflict
nodes.detail: Do not reset the project directory, clear the marker, overwrite a human file, or retry an already committed write. Finalization recovery is checked separately. A genuinely absent output needs a fresh typed preview and its own approval.

nodes.title: Use the result through task-scoped selection
nodes.body:
Context knowledge feeds the existing feature, fix, test-change and reviewer callers. They select current relevant inputs and deliver them to each actual actor.
A successful context write or initialized marker is not task authorization, current command proof, or evidence that a child loaded those inputs.

panels.title: 01  /  PICK THE EXISTING OWNER
panels.caption: Initial population, initialized refresh and interrupted-operation recovery are not interchangeable entries.

panels.title: 02  /  ACQUIRE BOUNDED EVIDENCE BEFORE SYNTHESIS
panels.caption: A missing qualified profile blocks dispatch. Complete returned reports and current snapshots are prerequisites, not optional best effort.

panels.title: 03  /  WRITE ONLY THROUGH THE DOCUMENT’S NATIVE CONTRACT
panels.caption: Five content documents have paired v2 provenance. An approval for one exact preview does not approve another document or finalization.

panels.title: 04  /  COMPLETE THE SELECTED LIFECYCLE, NOT A DIFFERENT ONE
panels.caption: Initial finalization and initialized refresh have different completion evidence. Recovery inspects native outcomes before a new write.

notes.text: A current hash is an identity check, not semantic approval. “Not found in this scope” is not a claim of universal absence.
Each pair is transactional; independent successful pairs are not a claim that the entire context set became visible atomically.
Source-delivery exception and open live qualification remain distinct from these implemented source contracts. No blanket host-readiness claim.
